GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; its initial x-y is a starting location that may remain or change by one rigid translation. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
DIAGNOSTIC OCCUPANCY: HIGH-FILL/CLOSE. Occupancy does not change placement permission. For every camera view, keep the product at its initial x-y or use one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation for a usable composition. Preserve exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never resize, reorient, reproject, redraw, crop, or occlude the product. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together.

Move the printer horizontally right by about one quarter of its own width, with no vertical movement or other change. This creates usable paper-sorting space on the left while leaving a generous visible margin at the right of the printer. Independently rebuild a dedicated pale oak printer table beneath this final position. Its top extends broadly to the left and provides a smaller supporting margin on the right; crop the furniture at the frame rather than the product. Fully support the base, with a narrow clear ledge in front. The printer sits square to the table, its back directly against the plain wall at the table's back edge. Keep the sorting area empty and standing access unobstructed.

Camera: Maintain the close, mildly elevated view in Image 1, looking gently downward with no camera roll: the printer's front dominates, with its top and narrow left side visible. Preserve the exact product projection and pixel dimensions despite the horizontal translation. Build the table and wall perspective around this unchanged view. The table's long edges rise slightly toward image right, and its depth edges recede toward the upper left. The operating front faces the near-camera standing approach, beyond the table's front edge.

Composition: The fully visible printer occupies the middle-right, retaining its original vertical placement. The pale oak table fills the lower middle plane, with a clear sorting surface beside the printer on the left, a smaller right-side clearance, and a narrow front ledge over a visible oak apron. The table's legs may be cropped by the lower frame. A plain dusty blue matte-painted wall fills the far plane across the full width above and beside the station. The printer's back touches this wall at the table's back edge, with nothing between them. No additional props or seating are needed. Soft daylight enters from upper left with generous neutral fill. The requested rightward move is feasible without changing product size or view; no requested object or requirement is omitted. Product translation and support reconstruction are independent.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
For every camera view, including close/high-fill views, keep the product at its initial location or reposition it using only one rigid image-plane x-y translation when that improves usable composition. This changes position only, not the product view or size.

Preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the final product position; product and support need not move together. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead.

The only permitted product change is one rigid image-plane x-y translation. Keep its exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, perspective, projection, foreshortening, silhouette, aspect proportions, open/closed and powered state, finish, details, logo and display content. Do not rotate, mirror, resize, shear, warp, reproject, redraw or activate the product. Do not zoom, reframe or change the viewpoint in a way that alters the product.

At the chosen product position, compose a category- and scenario-appropriate support beneath its weight-bearing base. The support may change independently of the product's translation: do not preserve baseline product-to-edge distances, support top extents or absolute support-edge locations as requirements. Fully support the base without floating or overhang, with believable front, back and side clearances, natural weight-bearing contact, a contact shadow and material-appropriate reflections on the support.

Construct furniture around the unchanged product orientation. A printer must sit square to its support in 3D with usable access to its operating front. A printer must face a usable seating or working edge with clear access to its keyboard and display. Do not rotate the product or reveal a different face to fit the furniture. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.

Tiny props, thin partition frames, screen graphics, sky and lighting casts alone do not qualify. Keep the planned blue materials, visible extent and placement consistent; leave small props neutral by default. Explicit minimal-blue or no-blue requests override that default, as do explicit blue amounts or carriers. Keep the product's original color, finish, exact orientation/view, scale, details and full visibility. Every camera view permits only one optional rigid image-plane x-y translation.
